findings.description: The instance user-data script embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key in plaintext. User data is retrievable by principals with instance-describe access and the credentials are exposed in source control and deployment metadata, enabling unauthorized AWS API access.

No metadata_options block requires IMDSv2, so the instance permits the legacy IMDSv1 credential retrieval path. A server-side request forgery flaw in the web service could be used to obtain instance metadata or any role credentials later attached to the instance.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key. Its protection therefore depends on an account-level default outside this configuration, and it may be created unencrypted, exposing data if storage media or snapshots are accessed.

This snapshot is created from a volume for which encryption is not enforced. EBS snapshots inherit the source volume's encryption state, so this configuration can preserve the volume data in an unencrypted snapshot.

TCP port 22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, making remote administration reachable from every internet address once the host has public connectivity. This increases exposure to password/key attacks and exploitation of SSH service vulnerabilities.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. A compromised web host can use this unrestricted path for command-and-control communications or data exfiltration.

The bucket receiving VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. Sensitive network telemetry written to the bucket is not guaranteed to be encrypted at rest by this Terraform configuration.
